analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.5.26
key_insights: Futures are about unchanged to start the week (Nasdaq -15bps, Russell +15bps), with bonds muted (10yr unchanged) and WTI -1%, after NDX made a new all-time-high close on Friday.
Brazil is in focus: EWZ is +13% pre-market after Bolsonaro performed better than expected and holds a surprise lead heading into the runoff in three weeks.
PTC is +36% on Schneider Electric's all-cash takeout bid. The briefing cites both $23.7bn (intro) and about $22.6bn (news item). ADSK is +5% and PCOR +6% in sympathy.

INTC is -4% and TSM +2% (+3% in Taipei) after Musk confirmed 'just discussions' with TSMC about helping his Terafab chip venture run its Texas factories. A Culpium newsletter said TSMC may use Terafab as anchor client for a future Texas fab.

OpenAI plans to test image ads in ChatGPT in the U.S. later this month and is expanding measurement tools and partner integrations (Kochava plus 10 others). Measurement is the main constraint on bigger advertiser budgets.

GS semiconductor 3Q preview: after SOX fell 11% vs SPX +4% over two months on de-risking, GS sees a more constructive setup and upside to estimates across most sub-sectors. This contrasts with the cautious 2Q setup.

GS expects significant positive estimate revisions for SemiCap on pull-ins to WFE spending and visibility into 2028. In compute it sees upside for server CPUs and key ASIC programs on higher hyperscaler capex.
GS is favorable on analog, preferring names with the most industrial, aero/defense and datacenter exposure. In memory/storage it prefers HDDs and NAND because of no near-term supply additions.
GS tactical semiconductor ideas: upside for AMAT, STX, MCHP and downside for QCOM, KLAC, WDC.

Macro tape: 2yr 4.80%, 10yr 5.27%, 30yr 5.625%. WTI is $90.80 with Middle East exports back above pre-war levels in late September per Reuters. Yemen's government launched a campaign to retake Houthi-held territory.
European stress: France political and fiscal worries are intensifying, Spain called a snap election for November, the euro hit a 17-month low overnight and France-Germany 10yr spreads keep widening.

Light catalyst week: ISM Services today, FOMC minutes Wednesday, U of Mich sentiment Friday. Earnings before season starts: STZ Tuesday night, APLD Wednesday night, PEP Thursday morning, DAL Friday morning.

GS Prime: US fundamental L/S net leverage fell a third straight week to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and in the 2nd percentile of five-year history. US equities were modestly net bought on short covering in Macro Products, partly offset by single-stock shorting.

Prime flows: 8 of 11 sectors were net sold (Comm Svcs, Consumer Discretionary, Materials led) while Health Care was the most net bought on short covering. Semis saw demand uptick after MU earnings and the NVDA $150bn buyback increase, but the desk sees minimal willingness to chase the move higher.

Russell 2000 futures positioning is deeply depressed, with systematic exposure in the 7th percentile and record leveraged-fund shorts as of 9/22. Short covering has begun on softer PCE and NFP data, but GS says sustained outperformance needs durable relief in rates.

GS derivatives desk likes IWM and QQQ upside into Q3 earnings and midterms. It traded over 140mm of NDX Dec26 105%/115% up-and-out calls and also likes NDX over RTY and NDX upvar to isolate tech outperformance.

ETF flow color: SPX is on track to beat RTY for 7 straight weeks (longest since 2018), cybersecurity ETFs are on track for one of their best monthly inflows (+$950mm), and TLT hit an all-time low this week.

GS Baskets: Friday's softer payroll print lowered yields without sparking recession fears, which GS says leaves room for a catch-up rally in laggards given weak breadth and light positioning. It recommends GSPUBETA for high-beta upside and GSPUBETX (Beta-ex-AI pair) for beta management.

TMT specialists: semis regained footing (SOX +4% vs NDX +70bps) but investors showed 'wrong-way' reactions to prints (ACN up, muted MU, JBL fade). NDX's 12m forward multiple is below its multi-year average, and the debate is whether to fully recommit to the AI trade given rates, oil and midterms.

GS Q3 2026 earnings preview: consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y vs realized 33% in Q2. AI infrastructure beneficiaries account for over 50% of EPS growth and consensus hyperscaler capex growth is 116%. GS expects most companies to beat.

Median S&P 500 stock EPS growth is expected to slow from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Input costs likely limit sequential margin expansion and the dollar is a smaller revenue tailwind. Tariff refunds were $77bn in Q2 and $69bn in Q3, roughly 6% of pre-tax profits each quarter.
GS analysts expect hyperscaler cloud revenue growth to accelerate from 48% in Q2 to 55% in Q3.

SIA data: August IC unit shipments ex-memory rose about 2% m/m, better than seasonal. Shipments run 10% above long-term trend on a three-month average (7% in July). Analog is about 10% above trend while MCU is 21.3% below trend, which GS attributes to consumer electronics softness.

STX and WDC fell 10%-11% Friday on reports that Toshiba will double nearline HDD capacity by end of FY27 (about ¥60bn Philippines investment) and aims to triple HDD market share to 30% from about 11%. A 65TB drive is targeted for 2030.

GS keeps a Sell on Adobe ahead of Anil Chakravarthy becoming CEO on 12/1 (Wadhwani leaving, permanent CFO pending). GS sees new leadership as a catalyst but wants visibility on strategic decisions and execution as competition intensifies.

GS upgraded Z.AI (Zhipu, 2513.HK) to Buy from Neutral with a HK$1,560 target (prior HK$1,610), citing raised 2026E year-end ARR of US$3.2bn (prior US$2.7bn). Shares are down 70% since July, now below US$40bn market cap, trading at 12X P/2026E year-end ARR vs 9X for MiniMax.
Street actions: MSFT upgraded to Buy (Melius), GFS downgraded to Neutral (BNP Paribas), HUBS downgraded to Market Perform (Raymond James), IOT initiated at Buy (Jefferies).

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth: consensus est +27% y/y vs realized +33% in Q2 (excluding some accounting distortions). Season starts the week of October 12 and about 70% of S&P 500 market cap reports by end of October.
Median S&P 500 stock EPS growth: consensus est slows from +14% in Q2 to +9% in Q3. GS expects most companies to beat consensus again.
AI infrastructure beneficiaries make up over 50% of consensus S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, alongside consensus hyperscaler capex growth of 116%.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth was 48% in Q2 (reported). GS analysts forecast 55% in Q3.
Tariff refunds boosted earnings by $77bn in Q2 and $69bn in Q3 (GS estimates), roughly 6% of US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter.
Upcoming prints: STZ Tuesday night, APLD Wednesday night, PEP Thursday morning, DAL Friday morning. PENG reports after close Tuesday and Tata Consultancy Services reports before the open Thursday.
Recent prints cited by the TMT desk: ACN reacted up, MU reaction was muted despite a solid print, and JBL faded.
